c: ELSE — An ELSE branch runs when its IF condition is false.
An IF/ELSEIF/ELSE chain checks conditions from top to bottom, and only the first matching branch runs. For mark = 74, mark >= 80 is false but mark >= 60 is true: Silver is the only output.
Nested selection places an IF inside another IF. First run the outer decision; the inner test is checked only when execution enters its branch.
Mutually exclusive branches is used for a specific reason: Only one matching route of an IF/ELSEIF/ELSE chain runs.

m.q: A program awards Gold for mark >= 80, Silver for 60–79 and Bronze otherwise. Trace marks 74 and 85, explaining why only one message prints. [4 marks]
st: Test IF mark >= 80 before ELSEIF mark >= 60.
74 fails the first test and passes the second, so prints Silver. [2]
85 passes the first test, so prints Gold and skips the remaining branches. [1]
Only the first matching IF/ELSEIF/ELSE branch executes. [1]

w: An online shop prints Free delivery if total >= 30 and Delivery charged otherwise. Trace total = 24. [2 marks]
24 >= 30 is false [1]; ELSE runs and prints Delivery charged [1].
A ride prints Adult for age >= 18, Teen for age >= 13, and Child otherwise. Trace age = 15. [2 marks]
15 fails >= 18 and satisfies >= 13 [1], so Teen prints [1].
A nested IF first checks mark >= 40. If true it checks mark >= 80 to print Gold or Pass; if false it prints Retry. Trace marks 90 and 25 and explain the nesting. [4 marks]
90 prints Gold [1]; 25 prints Retry [1]. The inner >=80 test is reached only if >=40 is true [1], so a failed mark does not enter that branch [1].
wSteps: Gold and Retry [2]; inner test only reached after outer Yes [2].

k.q: Predict the exact output of this OCR ERL program, change one value, then extend the program.
k.code:
mark = 74
if mark >= 80 then
    print("Gold")
elseif mark >= 60 then
    print("Silver")
else
    print("Bronze")
endif
p: Predict the output of the supplied code.
Change mark to 85 and predict the output.
Add a further elseif mark >= 40 then branch printing "Pass" before else.
k.a:
Original output: Silver.

After the changes: At 85: Gold. With new branch, a mark of 50 prints Pass.

Recheck the calculation and indentation using OCR ERL.

e:
IF mark >= 80 prints Gold; ELSEIF mark >= 60 prints Silver; ELSE prints Bronze. What happens for mark = 74? [2 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.
The mark fails >=80 but meets >=60 [1], so Silver is printed [1].

Write an IF/ELSEIF/ELSE structure assigning a ticket price: £4 if age < 12, £7 if 12–17, otherwise £10. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.
IF age < 12 THEN price = 4 [1]; ELSEIF age < 18 THEN price = 7 [1]; ELSE price = 10 [1]; ENDIF [1].

Write nested IF pseudocode: mark < 40 prints Retry; a pass of 40–79 prints Pass; 80+ prints Gold. Explain why only one output is produced. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.
Outer IF mark >= 40 [1]; nested IF mark >= 80 [1]; inner true prints Gold [1]; inner ELSE prints Pass [1]; outer ELSE prints Retry [1]; only the reached branch prints for each input [1].

priorExam.q: A cinema age check needs to work correctly. Explain how if and comparison would help. [4 marks]
priorExam.a: IF [1] — An IF block executes its instructions only when the condition is true. [1]. Comparison [1] — The Boolean test must compare values rather than assign a new value. [1].

ido.question: A workshop charges £0 under age 6, £3 for ages 6–15, and £8 otherwise. Choose a fee from an integer age and display it.
ido.scaffold:
if _____ then
    fee = _____
elseif _____ then
    fee = _____
else
    fee = _____
endif
print(_____)

steps.title: First age band
steps.explanation: The first true condition assigns the free price.

steps.title: Next unmatched band
steps.explanation: After the first branch fails, age < 16 covers ages 6–15.
steps.code:
if age < 6 then
    fee = 0
elseif age < 16 then
    fee = 3

steps.title: Else handles adults
steps.explanation: ELSE covers all remaining values; only one branch runs.
steps.code:
if age < 6 then
    fee = 0
elseif age < 16 then
    fee = 3
else
    fee = 8
endif

steps.title: Print the selected fee
steps.code:
if age < 6 then
    fee = 0
elseif age < 16 then
    fee = 3
else
    fee = 8
endif
print(fee)

wedo.question: A climbing club charges £0 under 5, £6 for ages 5–17, £10 otherwise. Use integer age and print price.
wedo.scaffold:
if _____ then
    price = _____
elseif _____ then
    price = _____
else
    price = _____
endif
print(_____)

steps.title: Under-five group
steps.explanation: The first condition is checked before any other.

steps.title: Second age band
steps.explanation: ELSEIF is only checked if the first IF is false.
steps.code:
if age < 5 then
    price = 0
elseif age < 18 then
    price = 6

steps.title: Complete all branches
steps.explanation: ELSE and ENDIF complete selection; output once.
steps.code:
if age < 5 then
    price = 0
elseif age < 18 then
    price = 6
else
    price = 10
endif
print(price)
